subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: Should OpenClaw treat aborted no-output embedded agent results as fallback-worthy for GitHub Copilot isolated cron runs, or keep the fix transport-specific until live proof identifies a safer boundary?
rationale: The current classifier intentionally excludes aborted results, and broadening that rule could retry after partial tool side effects; source inspection alone cannot choose that product/runtime policy.

options.title: Transport-Specific Boundary
options.body: Add live-proven Copilot Anthropic first-token or progress timeout handling and keep generic aborted-result fallback conservative.

options.title: Generic No-Output Fallback
options.body: Allow aborted no-output embedded results to trigger configured fallback when there is no committed delivery evidence, accepting broader retry semantics.

options.title: Document The Workaround
options.body: Document using a non-Anthropic Copilot primary and leave fallback behavior unchanged until more live evidence is available.

recommendation.title: Transport-Specific Boundary
recommendation.body: Add live-proven Copilot Anthropic first-token or progress timeout handling and keep generic aborted-result fallback conservative.

likelyOwner.reason: Most connected to the current fallback classifier wiring and Copilot provider snapshot among the inspected history.
